text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Iraqi press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
QADISSIYA
- President Saddam Hussein says Iraq to make big steps in economic development.
- Iraq's oil minister reviews economic and energy cooperation with Italy in Rome.
- Constant flow of trucks carrying foodstuffs under oil-for-food deal reaches Iraq from both Turkish and Jordanian borders.
- Washington Post says U.S. backed down in the face of Iraqi insistence to fly helicopters through no-fly zones.
- Preparations under way to receive Iraq's Moslem pilgrims.
- Ministry of industry and minerals decides to sell products direct to citizens.
- Massacre in Algeria claims 93 lives.
- France does not object to the flying of Iraqi helicopters in air-exclusion areas.
- Deputy Prime Minister Tareq Aziz receives senior Russian MP.
- Vice-President receives French diplomat in Baghdad.
(The above were also carried by THAWRA and AL-IRAQ)
- Editorial warns Washington that Iraq will not remain idle if attacked.
- Article on Saddam's birthday celebrations.
THAWRA
- Commentary says Washington no longer capable of mobilising U.N. Security Council against Iraq.
- Article on role of multinational companies in the sabotage of Third World economies.
- Article on what needs to be done to normalise ties with Iran.
AL-IRAQ
- Article says Iraq's mother of battles (1991 Gulf War over Kuwait) was the start of a new balance in world relations.
